$comment: How a worker resolves the citations in a text it generated under `cite`, as every worker must resolve them. The model was asked to wrap the words of each claim in a token naming the source it rests on: `[[<resourceId>: <claim>]]`, or `[[<resourceId>/<annotationId>: <claim>]]` where the passage it read came from an annotation. A token is transport, never content: every token is taken out of the text, a marked token leaving its claim where it stood and a bare token its source's name, and each citation that names what the context really showed becomes a citation of exactly those words. Nothing is guessed. THE TOKENS. A token is bare or marked. A BARE token is `[[`, an id, optionally `/` and a second id, then `]]`, where an id is one or more characters none of which is white space, `[`, `]` or `/`. A MARKED token is `[[`, one or more citations separated by commas, `:`, then its claim up to the first `]]` after the `:`, which ends it; a citation is an id, optionally `/` and a second id, where an id is one or more characters none of which is white space, `[`, `]`, `/`, `,` or `:`, and white space may stand on either side of a comma. Anything else in double brackets is no token and stays in the text. Tokens are taken left to right, and one that can be read as marked is marked. A MARKED token whose claim is not empty is replaced by its CLAIM: what stands between its `:` and its `]]`, less the white space at its ends. Each of its citations cites the claim, in the order the token lists them. A BARE token is replaced by its source's NAME, the one `contextNames` holds for its first id, written as `format` writes it (below), and its citation cites the name as written. A marked token whose claim is empty is taken as bare tokens are, one for each of its citations, in order, each put where the one before it ended. Where a token puts something in its place, the text since the token before it is kept as it is. Where it puts nothing, that text is kept less the run of spaces and tabs at its very end; a line end is neither, so spaces that stand before a line end are not at the end and are kept with it. The text after the last token is kept as it is. What a token puts in the text is never read for tokens. A citation makes none, and is `dropped`, when its first id is not a ResourceId (specs/src/identifiers/kinds.json) or is not one of `contextResourceIds`; when it has a second id and that id is not an AnnotationId (the same file) or is not one of `contextAnnotationIds`; or, of a bare token, when `contextNames` holds no name for its source: the token then puts nothing in its place. A marked token's claim stays in the text whether any of its citations cites it or none does. What a model invents is never linked, and no id is ever written into the text as a name. THE NAME. `format` is the media type the text is written in: text/plain, text/markdown, or application/pdf, whose text is the Typst source the model wrote. In text/plain a name is written as it is. In text/markdown and in application/pdf each of its ASCII punctuation characters, the 32 of `!"#$%&'()*+,-./:;<=>?@[\]^_`{|}~`, is written after a backslash, which both read as that character itself, so that no part of a name is read as markup wherever it stands. No other character is. `start` and `end` are offsets in the resolved text, counting its code points (specs/src/text/offset-cases.json), a character outside the Basic Multilingual Plane being one; `exact` is the text between them, so a name's citation quotes the name as written, backslashes and all; and `annotationId` is the citation's second id where it had one. `dropped` lists the first id of each dropped citation, in order: the worker logs a warning for each. White space is what Unicode gives the White_Space property; no case rests on U+0085 or U+FEFF, about which implementations disagree. `contexts` holds which ids a gathered context makes citable, and the names it gives them. `resourceIds`, a set: its focus resource (for a focus that is an annotation, the resource the annotation is in), every node of its graph that is a resource, the resource of every semantically similar passage, and every key of a resource focus's related content. `annotationIds`, a set: the annotation of every semantically similar passage that came from one, and no other: not the annotation a focus is, and not an annotation among the graph's nodes. `names`, from a resource id to its name: the first name the context gives the resource, read in the order the focus's `name`, a graph node's `label`, a similar passage's `resourceName`, that is more than white space and more than the resource's id, less the white space at its ends. A key of the related content gives none. So a resource the context names only by its id, as the Librarian labels a citer whose view it could not read, has no name: a bare token cannot cite it, and a marked one can. Neither set nor `names` has an entry where there is no context. Every worker runs every case against its resolving of citation tokens and its collecting of the ids a model may cite, in whatever language it is written. Add a case here before changing an implementation.

cases.why: a bare token is replaced by its source's name where it stood, the space before it kept, and its citation is exactly that name: nothing is guessed
cases.text: Paris is the capital of France, as [[ctx-9]] says.

resolved.text: Paris is the capital of France, as Context Doc says.

cases.why: a bare token after a finished sentence is replaced all the same: the text reads as a fragment, and the link is on the name
cases.text: Paris is the capital of France. [[ctx-9]] It is large.

resolved.text: Paris is the capital of France. Context Doc It is large.

cases.why: the name is the context's, never the model's: a name written in a token is no id the context showed, and the token is taken out and cites nothing
two bare tokens are two names, each cited where it was put
a bare token that names an annotation the context showed carries that annotation's id, and is replaced by its resource's name
an id the context did not hold is a model's invention: the token is taken out with the space before it, puts nothing in its place, and cites nothing
a dropped token is taken out like any other, and a later name's positions are in the text without it
what is not a resource id is never cited, even where the context's related content is keyed by it
a bare token needs no text before it: it is its source's name wherever it stands

resolved.text: Rome was founded on seven hills.

cases.why: double brackets around white space, around more than two ids, or around nothing are no token, and stay in the text
tabs before a token that puts nothing in its place are taken out with the spaces
spaces and tabs before a token that is replaced by a name stay: the name takes the token's place
a line feed before a token is not taken out with it
spaces that stand before a line feed are not at the end of the text before a token that puts nothing in its place: they stay in the text with the line feed
a source the context gave no name, as it gives none to a resource it names only by its id, has none to put in a bare token's place: the token is taken out with the space before it, and cites nothing
a marked token cites a source the context gave no name as it cites any other: a marked claim needs no name
a text with no token is left as it is
positions count the text's characters, not its bytes
positions count the text's code points, not its UTF-16 code units: after an emoji, a name with an emoji in it starts at 10 and ends at 21, where a count of code units would say 11 and 23
a token that names an annotation the context did not show makes no citation, though its resource is one the context showed; a later token for the resource alone is its name

resolved.text: Ice melts. Salt dissolves in Rome.

cases.why: what is not an annotation id is never cited, even where the context names it
in Markdown a name's ASCII punctuation is written after a backslash, so that none of it is read as markup; the citation is of the name as written, backslashes and all
in Markdown every one of the 32 ASCII punctuation characters is written after a backslash
in a PDF's source, which is Typst, every one of the 32 ASCII punctuation characters is written after a backslash, as in Markdown
in plain text a name is written as it is
only ASCII punctuation is written after a backslash: a curly quotation mark or a dash outside ASCII is written as it is
a name is put in the text and never read for tokens: a name that holds double brackets is no token
a marked token's claim stays in the text where the token was, with the space before it, and its citation is exactly the claim: nothing is guessed
cases.text: The theory was [[r1: proposed by Smith]].

resolved.text: The theory was proposed by Smith.

cases.why: a mark inside a sentence cites what it wraps and nothing more
a marked claim with an abbreviation, a file name, a decimal and a full stop of its own is cited whole: no sentence is read in it
cases.text: [[r1: Dr. Lovelace edited config.json at 3.14 a.m.]] Then she left.

resolved.text: Dr. Lovelace edited config.json at 3.14 a.m. Then she left.

citations.exact: Dr. Lovelace edited config.json at 3.14 a.m.

cases.why: a marked claim of two sentences is cited whole
a token that lists several ids cites its claim once for each, over the one span, in the order it lists them
white space may stand on either side of the comma between two ids
an id of a marked token that the context did not show cites nothing: the claim stays, and the token's other ids cite it
a marked token none of whose ids the context showed leaves its claim in the text, and cites nothing
what is not a resource id is never cited from a marked token either, and its claim stays
a marked token names the annotation a passage came from as a bare one does
a marked token whose claim is empty is taken as a bare token: it is its source's name
a marked token whose claim is empty and that lists several ids is taken as as many bare tokens, each put where the one before it ended: their names stand together
a claim ends at the first ]] after its colon: what follows stays in the text
the white space at the ends of a claim is the token's, and leaves the text with it: the claim is its words
a marked claim may run over a line end
a marked claim's offsets count code points: after an emoji it starts at 2, where a count of UTF-16 code units says 3
a bare token after a marked one is its source's name, as a bare token always is

resolved.text: Alpha holds, as Tea Notes says.

cases.why: a marked token with no closing ]] is no token, and stays in the text as it is
a token inside a claim is no token of its own: the claim ends at the first ]], what was inside it is the claim's, and what follows stays in the text

contexts.why: a resource focus: the focus itself, the graph's resources (not its annotations), the resources of similar passages, and the keys of the related content; the one annotation a similar passage came from, which the graph's annotation is not; and the name of each but the related content's key, which brings none

related.res-4: The text of a related resource.

contexts.why: an annotation focus: the resource the annotation is in, with its name, and no annotation: the focus is not one the model was shown an id for
no context at all: nothing can be cited, and nothing is named

a resource the context names more than once is named by the first name it gives, in the order the focus, the graph, the similar passages; a name that is only the resource's id is passed over for a later one

a resource the context names only by its id has no name, as the Librarian labels a citer whose view it could not read; nor has one named by white space alone; and the white space at a name's ends is no part of it, nor of what is held to the id
